headline: Israeli military forces advance into central Gaza amid evacuation warnings
standfirst: Israeli ground forces have launched a rare incursion into part of central Gaza outside their control, prompting renewed displacement and severe regional condemnation.
keyPoints: Israeli tanks and troops advanced east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza.
The military stated the operation targeted a tunnel posing an immediate threat to troops.
Hamas condemned the move as a flagrant violation of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
Numerous residents were forced to flee their shelters along the Salah al-Din road.

paragraphs: Israeli ground forces launched a rare military operation on Wednesday into a portion of the central Gaza Strip that remains outside their usual control. Tanks rolled east of the Nuseirat refugee camp and onto the territory's primary north-to-south thoroughfare, accompanied by heavy artillery bombardments and gunfire. The incursion affected areas near the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps, prompting urgent evacuation warnings from military authorities.

Prior to the advance, the military liaison agency issued explicit warnings telling local inhabitants and aid organisations to stay away from the designated zone for their own safety. A section of the Salah al-Din road passing through the affected area was closed entirely to civilian traffic. Residents described intense shelling and chaotic scenes as families abandoned temporary shelters and fled on foot or via donkey carts.

Footage verified by independent monitors captured individuals running along the road amid the sounds of nearby artillery and automatic weapon fire. Civil defence officials reported that separate drone strikes across different parts of the territory resulted in additional casualties, while witnesses spoke of widespread destruction. The operation marked a significant escalation in an area where relative ceasefire lines had been observed for months.

sections.heading: Background and context of the fragile truce
paragraphs: The latest military activity occurs against the backdrop of a prolonged conflict that began with the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel in October 2023. That initial assault resulted in substantial casualties and the abduction of numerous hostages, triggering an extensive military campaign across the Palestinian territory. A subsequent ceasefire brokered by the United States came into effect in October 2025, establishing the Yellow Line to separate areas controlled by Israeli forces from the remainder of the enclave.

Despite the cessation of major hostilities, sporadic violence and near-daily strikes have persisted over the past thirteen months. Approximately ninety percent of Gaza's population remains displaced, with the vast majority living in makeshift tents and rudimentary shelters due to widespread infrastructural damage. Reconstruction efforts have faced severe delays while international peace proposals aimed at achieving a lasting disarmament and withdrawal framework remain stalled.

sections.heading: Positions of the involved parties
paragraphs: The military authorities defended the incursion as a precise and necessary measure to dismantle a dangerous infrastructure network west of the Yellow Line. Officials stated that the operation was conducted jointly with domestic security services to remove an immediate threat to deployed troops and prevent hostile activities. They maintained that forces operate in accordance with existing agreements to thwart any attempts to harm personnel or civilians.

Conversely, the Palestinian group governing the remainder of the territory strongly denounced the advance as a dangerous escalation. Hamas officials stated that the military movement constituted a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement and proved that the occupation had abandoned its commitments. Local residents expressed profound fear that the operation might herald a broader resumption of widespread warfare and displacement.

sections.heading: Wider humanitarian and political impact
paragraphs: The humanitarian situation for the enclave's 2.1 million residents continues to deteriorate amid ongoing security operations and restrictions on movement. International bodies have repeatedly highlighted the dire conditions faced by displaced families who lack adequate shelter, sanitation, and medical supplies ahead of winter months. The breakdown of structured reconstruction plans leaves communities vulnerable to recurring cycles of displacement and acute hardship.

Politically, the timing of the escalation coincides with a sensitive domestic landscape in Israel, where political leaders have navigated complex coalition dynamics and leadership challenges. Security considerations and the enforcement of established demarcation lines remain central to domestic political discourse. Any sustained breach of the existing truce threatens to unravel fragile diplomatic frameworks designed to bring stability to the region.

sections.heading: Future outlook and developments
paragraphs: Uncertainty surrounds the immediate duration and scope of the ongoing ground operation in the central sector. Military planners have indicated that forces will remain deployed until perceived threats are fully neutralized, leaving open the possibility of extended engagement. Observers will monitor whether localized skirmishes escalate into a broader breakdown of the existing cessation of hostilities.

Diplomatic channels face renewed pressure from international mediators striving to prevent further deterioration of the truce framework. The ultimate fate of stalled peace initiatives hinges on whether both sides can reach consensus regarding disarmament and troop withdrawals. Meanwhile, civilian populations caught in the crossfire continue to bear the immediate humanitarian toll of the unresolved political impasse.

highlight: The Israeli military said the targeted operation aimed to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the so-called Yellow Line.
socialSummary: Israeli forces launch a rare ground operation in central Gaza beyond the Yellow Line, drawing fierce condemnation from Hamas.
